title.sl: Znam, lahko: I can, I can't
title.it: Potere, sapere: I can, I can't

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj kdo zna in česa ne (I can, she can't), vprašaš Can you …? s kratkimi odgovori, prosiš in dovoliš s can, vljudno pa vprašaš Could you …, please?
goal.de: Du sagst, was jemand kann und nicht kann (I can, she can't), fragst Can you …? mit kurzen Antworten, bittest und erlaubst mit can und fragst höflich Could you …, please?
goal.it: Dici che cosa qualcuno sa o può fare e che cosa no (I can, she can't), chiedi Can you …? con le risposte brevi, chiedi e permetti con can e chiedi con gentilezza Could you …, please?
goal.en: You can say what people can and can't do (I can, she can't), ask Can you …? with short answers, ask and allow with can, and ask politely: Could you …, please?

say.sl: **can** pove, kaj kdo zna ali zmore: **I can swim.** (Znam plavati.) **Jack can run fast.** (Jack zna hitro teči.) Za vse osebe je enak, brez -s: **she can**, nikoli *she cans*. Glagol za njim je brez **to**: **He can drive.** (Zna voziti.), ne *can to drive*.
say.de: **can** sagt, was jemand kann: **I can swim.** (Ich kann schwimmen.) **Jack can run fast.** (Jack kann schnell laufen.) Es ist für alle Personen gleich, ohne -s: **she can**, nie *she cans*. Das Verb danach hat kein **to**: **He can drive.** (Er kann Auto fahren.), nicht *can to drive*.
say.it: **can** dice che cosa qualcuno sa o riesce a fare: **I can swim.** (So nuotare.) **Jack can run fast.** (Jack sa correre veloce.) È uguale per tutte le persone, senza -s: **she can**, mai *she cans*. Il verbo dopo non ha **to**: **He can drive.** (Sa guidare.), non *can to drive*.
say.en: **can** says what someone is able to do: **I can swim.** **Jack can run fast.** It is the same for every person, with no -s: **she can** (never *she cans*). The verb after it has no **to**: **He can drive.** (never *He can to drive.*)

examples.de: Mr Dixon kann an einem Tag ein Tor machen.

say.sl: Zanikano je **can't**, v celoti **cannot**, v eni besedi: **I can't swim.** (Ne znam plavati.) **Sam can't come today.** (Sam danes ne more priti.) **I can't find my keys!** (Ne najdem ključev!) Napisano pogosto **cannot**, v govoru **can't**.
say.de: Verneint heißt es **can't**, ausgeschrieben **cannot**, in einem Wort: **I can't swim.** (Ich kann nicht schwimmen.) **Sam can't come today.** (Sam kann heute nicht kommen.) **I can't find my keys!** (Ich finde meine Schlüssel nicht!) Geschrieben oft **cannot**, gesprochen **can't**.
say.it: La negazione è **can't**, per intero **cannot**, una parola sola: **I can't swim.** (Non so nuotare.) **Sam can't come today.** (Sam oggi non può venire.) **I can't find my keys!** (Non trovo le chiavi!) Per iscritto spesso **cannot**, a voce **can't**.
say.en: The negative is **can't**, in full **cannot**, one word: **I can't swim.** **Sam can't come today.** **I can't find my keys!** Written often **cannot**, spoken **can't**.

examples.sl: Meg ne zna plezati po drevesih.

examples.it: Meg non sa arrampicarsi sugli alberi.

examples.it: Il vecchio Wilf ora non riesce più a salire sul monte, ma sa raccontare una bella storia.

say.sl: V vprašanju gre **can** na začetek, brez do: **Can you swim?** (Znaš plavati?) **Can Jack drive?** (Zna Jack voziti?) Kratki odgovor: **Yes, I can.** (Ja, znam.) **No, he can't.** (Ne, ne zna.) Nikoli *Do you can …?*
say.de: In der Frage steht **can** vorn, ohne do: **Can you swim?** (Kannst du schwimmen?) **Can Jack drive?** (Kann Jack Auto fahren?) Die Kurzantwort: **Yes, I can.** (Ja.) **No, he can't.** (Nein.) Nie *Do you can …?*
say.it: Nella domanda **can** va all'inizio, senza do: **Can you swim?** (Sai nuotare?) **Can Jack drive?** (Jack sa guidare?) La risposta breve: **Yes, I can.** (Sì.) **No, he can't.** (No.) Mai *Do you can …?*
say.en: A question puts **can** first, with no do: **Can you swim?** (never *Do you can swim?*) **Can Jack drive?** The short answer: **Yes, I can.** **No, he can't.**

say.sl: S **can** tudi prosiš in dovoliš: **Can I help?** (Lahko pomagam?) **Can you help me?** (Mi lahko pomagaš?) **You can sit here.** (Lahko sedeš sem.) **You can't park here.** (Tu ne smeš parkirati.) Za znati, moči in smeti reče angleščina **can**.
say.de: Mit **can** bittest und erlaubst du auch: **Can I help?** (Kann ich helfen?) **Can you help me?** (Kannst du mir helfen?) **You can sit here.** (Du kannst dich hier hinsetzen.) **You can't park here.** (Hier darfst du nicht parken.) Für können und dürfen sagt Englisch oft nur **can**.
say.it: Con **can** chiedi e permetti anche: **Can I help?** (Posso aiutare?) **Can you help me?** (Mi puoi aiutare?) **You can sit here.** (Puoi sederti qui.) **You can't park here.** (Qui non puoi parcheggiare.) Per sapere e potere l'inglese dice **can**.
say.en: **can** also asks and allows: **Can I help?** (an offer) **Can you help me?** (asking) **You can sit here.** (it is allowed) **You can't park here.** (it isn't)

say.sl: Še bolj vljudno vprašaš s **could**: **Could you open the gate, please?** (Bi lahko odprli vrata, prosim?) **Could I have the bill, please?** (Lahko prosim račun?) Gospod Tyson ima rad **Could I …?** Odgovor je pogosto **Of course.** (Seveda.) ali **Yes, sure.** (Ja, lahko.)
say.de: Höflicher fragst du mit **could**: **Could you open the gate, please?** (Könnten Sie bitte das Tor aufmachen?) **Could I have the bill, please?** (Könnte ich bitte die Rechnung haben?) Mr Tyson hört gern **Could I …?** Die Antwort ist oft **Of course.** (Natürlich.) oder **Yes, sure.** (Ja, klar.)
say.it: Per chiedere con più gentilezza usi **could**: **Could you open the gate, please?** (Potrebbe aprire il cancello, per favore?) **Could I have the bill, please?** (Potrei avere il conto, per favore?) A Mr Tyson piace **Could I …?** La risposta è spesso **Of course.** (Certo.) o **Yes, sure.** (Sì, certo.)
say.en: To ask more politely, say **could**: **Could you open the gate, please?** **Could I have the bill, please?** Mr Tyson likes **Could I …?** The answer is often **Of course.** or **Yes, sure.**

summary.sl: **can** + glagol brez to, za vse osebe enako: **I can swim**, **she can drive** (nikoli *cans*, *can to*). Zanikano **can't** (**cannot**). Vprašanje brez do: **Can you …?** **Yes, I can.** **No, I can't.** S **can** tudi prosiš in dovoliš: **Can I help?** **You can sit here.** Bolj vljudno: **Could you …, please?**
summary.de: **can** + Verb ohne to, für alle gleich: **I can swim**, **she can drive** (nie *cans*, *can to*). Verneint **can't** (**cannot**). Die Frage ohne do: **Can you …?** **Yes, I can.** **No, I can't.** Mit **can** bittest und erlaubst du auch: **Can I help?** **You can sit here.** Höflicher: **Could you …, please?**
summary.it: **can** + il verbo senza to, uguale per tutti: **I can swim**, **she can drive** (mai *cans*, *can to*). Negazione **can't** (**cannot**). La domanda senza do: **Can you …?** **Yes, I can.** **No, I can't.** Con **can** chiedi e permetti anche: **Can I help?** **You can sit here.** Più gentile: **Could you …, please?**
summary.en: **can** + the verb without to, the same for everyone: **I can swim**, **she can drive** (never *cans*, *can to*). No: **can't** (**cannot**). A question without do: **Can you …?** **Yes, I can.** **No, I can't.** **can** also asks and allows: **Can I help?** **You can sit here.** More polite: **Could you …, please?**

exercises.text: Mrs Birkett ___ cook for forty people at the inn. Brewer Sam ___ (not) cook at all, but he makes very good ale. — ___ I help you, Mrs Birkett? — Oh yes, thank you! ___ you take these cups to the kitchen, please? — Of course. And I ___ wash them, too.

translation.sl: Gospa Birkett zna v gostilni skuhati za štirideset ljudi. Pivovar Sam sploh ne zna kuhati, dela pa zelo dobro pivo. — Vam lahko pomagam, gospa Birkett? — O ja, hvala! Lahko odneseš te skodelice v kuhinjo, prosim? — Seveda. Lahko jih tudi pomijem.
translation.de: Mrs Birkett kann im Gasthaus für vierzig Leute kochen. Brauer Sam kann überhaupt nicht kochen, aber er braut sehr gutes Bier. — Kann ich Ihnen helfen, Mrs Birkett? — Oh ja, danke! Könntest du bitte diese Tassen in die Küche bringen? — Natürlich. Und ich kann sie auch abwaschen.
translation.it: Mrs Birkett sa cucinare per quaranta persone alla locanda. Il birraio Sam non sa cucinare per niente, ma fa una birra molto buona. — Posso aiutarla, Mrs Birkett? — Oh sì, grazie! Potresti portare queste tazze in cucina, per favore? — Certo. E posso anche lavarle.
translation.en: Mrs Birkett can cook for forty people at the inn. Brewer Sam can't cook at all, but he makes very good ale. — Can I help you, Mrs Birkett? — Oh yes, thank you! Could you take these cups to the kitchen, please? — Of course. And I can wash them, too.

translation.sl: Gospod Dixon zna narediti ograjna vrata in podkve. — Mi lahko naredite vrata za pašnik, gospod Dixon? — Ja, lahko. Ampak ta teden jih ne morem narediti. Lahko pridete nazaj naslednji teden?
translation.de: Mr Dixon kann Tore und Hufeisen machen. — Können Sie mir ein Tor für meine Weide machen, Mr Dixon? — Ja. Aber diese Woche kann ich es nicht machen. Können Sie nächste Woche wiederkommen?
translation.it: Mr Dixon sa fare cancelli e ferri di cavallo. — Può farmi un cancello per il mio campo, Mr Dixon? — Sì. Ma questa settimana non posso farlo. Può tornare la settimana prossima?
translation.en: Mr Dixon can make gates and horseshoes. — Can you make a gate for my field, Mr Dixon? — Yes, I can. But I can't make it this week. Can you come back next week?
